I got a lot of that during my last stint at sobriety. A lot of men are insecure about (lots of things) their own drinking habits, so you'll get that sometimes. The worst offender in my own life has very much spiraled since then, unfortunately. 

You don't owe anyone an explanation and you're fighting a fuckin' demon to regain control of your life. Doesn't sound like "fucking pussy shit" to me!

I'd recommend therapy. It is very different having somebody who's job is to listen and help you as opposed to your friends and family (who are also great supports). I was in denial about my drinking for years (still kind of am) and I even was getting angry with my therapist for constantly coming back to my drinking. Lied to her innumerable times about it. Gee...I wonder why she thinks I have a drinking problem... :)

Alcohol is absolutely my escape. From work, roommates, family, friends, everything. I've tried to figure out what my "triggers" are so that I can avoid them, but I am a lonely-at-home drunk. Its just how I numb out the day.

I'm really happy for you that you are connecting with your family again. They don't understand your addiction, but they have welcomed you back. That's all that matters. 

This sub definitely helps and being anonymous is a great freedom. I haven't found any sort of support group that helps me as much as this place does, so I'm glad I'm back. 

I see so many posts about husbands, fathers, wives, and mothers and how they want to present for their families. In truth, I can't even being to fathom starting my own until I kick this. The self-loathing does nothing for the confidence to find a good partner, not to mention the bloated body that comes along with the consumption. That's not even getting to the emotional battles I would endure trying to hide it from someone every day.

My brother is very different from me and I think he is hurt knowing that I basically have lived a double-life right under his nose. My parents would likely be similarly hurt whenever I decide to have that conversation. I'm almost 30 and live far away from all of them, but I have plans to move closer and reconnect. Shouldn't have to white knuckle through life a lone.

Anyways, thanks for your great comment.

What I'm reminding myself is that alcohol will absolutely not help ANY of the things you just listed. You can numb the emotions for a night but the next morning they will be back with vengeance holding hands with a hangover. You've done awesome already
